subject: Handle cable coupling, a view
status: Technical concept illustration; not dimensioned or mechanically validated
neck_geometry: The stock silver neck is a rectangular prism with a square cross-section, flat faces, and sharp longitudinal edges; the orange cable-housing anchor grips its square profile, not a cylinder.
color_key: Only the original stock handle is blue in this crop. Added 3D-printed shaft clamp and trigger strap are orange. Stock shaft and wire remain silver; the moving trigger and cable housing remain black.

axes.y: up, parallel to the long reacher neck
axes.z: out of the page toward the viewer; negative z goes into the page

requirements: One close view of the specific blue handle, black moving squeeze trigger, and lower silver shaft; no phone, inset, or extra view.
A removable split clamp on the stationary lower shaft anchors the bicycle brake cable outer housing.
The exposed inner steel wire follows a continuous, visible path from the housing stop to a small removable tab strapped around the moving black trigger.
Squeezing the trigger pulls the inner wire relative to the fixed housing; keep the trigger and usable hand grip visible.
Use minimal extra metal parts, no drilled holes, no internal handle changes, and no attachment to the handle's existing screw holes.
This visible coupling is the one represented in full assembly image 1a.
Show a small x/y/z axis glyph on opaque white technical drawing paper, with positive z toward the viewer.
